conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I’m doing okay, thanks for asking! Just trying to keep things light, you know? How are you?

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: I'm here to help you with your experience today. Can you tell me about any feelings or thoughts you've had recently that stood out to you?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: The other day, I saw a news story that featured a similar situation to something I went through, and it hit me pretty hard. I found myself worrying a lot, and it kind of spiraled into me feeling like everything around me was a threat. It was just really unsettling.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds intense. How did that worry affect your activities or interactions in the hours after viewing the news story?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: After that story, I felt really on edge. I avoided going to places where there were a lot of people because I kept thinking something bad might happen. It felt safer to just stay home and distract myself instead of facing that anxiety head-on.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: Staying home can be a common response to feeling on edge. In those moments at home, how did you manage those feelings of anxiety?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: While I was at home, I kept myself busy with little tasks. I thought it would help, but it sort of turned into a way to escape from how I was really feeling. I didn’t want to face those anxious thoughts, so I just cleaned and organized things instead. It felt like a distraction, but deep down, I knew I wasn’t really dealing with it.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It sounds like you were trying to find some control through those tasks. After spending that time focused on distractions, how did you feel about your anxious thoughts later on?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Later on, I found that the anxious thoughts hadn’t really gone away; they were still lurking in the back of my mind. It made me feel a bit frustrated because I realized that just keeping busy didn’t help me confront what I was really feeling. I thought about how those worries might come back when I least expected them.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That frustration is understandable. In the hours since realizing those thoughts were still there, how have you been coping with the possibility of them returning?
